==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|legende}}, from {{der|en|fro|legende}}, from {{der|en|la-med|legenda||a legend, story, especially the lives of the saints}}, from {{der|en|la|legendus|legenda|things which ought to be read}}, from {{m|la|lego||to read}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛd͡ʒ.ənd/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈliːd͡ʒ.ənd/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-legend.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|en-au-legend.ogg|a=AU}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # The [[life story]] of a [[saint]] {{q|such stories are often [[embellish]]ed, but any kind is called a legend}}. #: {{ux|en|As a child she had nothing to read but the '''legends''' of early Christian martyrs.}} # {{senseid|en|story}} An unrealistic story depicting past events. ## A [[story]] of unknown origin describing plausible but [[extraordinary]] past [[event]]s. ##: {{syn|en|myth}} ##: {{ux|en|The '''legend''' of Troy was discovered to have a historical basis.}} ## A plausible story set in the historical past, but whose [[historicity]] is uncertain. ##: {{ux|en|the '''legend''' of Robin Hood}} ## A story in which a [[kernel of truth]] is [[embellish]]ed to an unlikely degree. ##: {{syn|en|myth|tall tale}} ##: {{ux|en|The 1984 Rose Bowl prank has spawned many '''legends'''. Here's the real story.}} ## A fabricated backstory for a [[spy]], with associated documents and records. ##: {{syn|en|cover story}} ##: {{ux|en|According to his '''legend''', he once worked for the Red Cross, spreading humanitarian aid in Africa.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=w:Ronald Kessler|title=Inside the CIA|page=115|publisher=w:Pocket Books|year_published=1994|isbn=067173458X |passage=If the documents are needed to establish "a light '''legend'''," meaning a superficial cover story, no steps are taken to make sure that if someone calls the college or motor vehicle department, the name on the document will be registered.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=Rodney Carlisle|title=[[w:Complete Idiot's Guides|The Complete Idiot's Guide to]] Spies and Espionage|page=105|publisher=w:Alpha Books|isbn=0028644182 |passage=Sorge solidified his own position by returning to Germany and developing a new '''legend'''. He joined the Nazi Party{{...}}.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=w:Curtis Peebles|title=Twilight Warriors|page=25|publisher=w:Naval Institute Press|isbn=1591146607 |passage=Both the agent's '''legend''' and documents were intended to stand up against casual questions from Soviet citizens, such as during a job interview, or a routine police document check, such as were made at railway stations.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} Such stories considered [[collectively]]; [[unverified]] [[traditional]] [[tale]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author={{w|Harry E. Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=212|passage=According to ancient '''legend''', a Greek girl, partaking of saffron for an entire week, could not resist a lover.}} # {{senseid|en|person}} A person related to a legend or legends. ## A leading [[protagonist]] in a historical legend. ##: {{syn|en|hero}} ##: {{ux|en|Achilles is a '''legend''' in Greek culture.}} ## A person of [[extraordinary]] [[fame]] or [[accomplishment]]s. ##: {{ux|en|Michael Jordan stands as a '''legend''' in basketball.}} ##: {{ux|en|Sachin Tendulkar stands as a '''legend''' in cricket.}} ### {{lb|en|UK|Irish|Australia|New Zealand|colloquial|slang}} A cool, nice or helpful person, ''especially'' one who is male. ###: {{syn|en|brick}} ###: {{ux|en|I've lost my pen! —Here mate, borrow mine. —You '''legend'''.}} # {{senseid|en|cartography}} {{lb|en|cartography}} A [[key]] to the symbols and color codes on a [[map]], [[chart]], etc. #: {{syn|en|guide|key}} #: {{ux|en|According to the '''legend''' on the map, that building is a school.}} # {{lb|en|numismatics|heraldry|nocat=y}} An [[inscription]], [[motto]], or title, especially one surrounding the field in a medal or coin, or placed upon a heraldic shield or beneath an engraving or illustration. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|title=AA Book of British Villages|publisher=Drive Publications Ltd|page=375, about [[Terling]]|text=Further clues are provided by milk-floats bearing the '''legend''' 'Lord Rayleigh's Dairies: A Family Business', and a number of signs indicating the whereabouts of various departments of Lord Rayleigh's Farms.}} #* {{RQ:Wolfe Urth|chapter=XLVIII|page=281|passage={{...}}there were three small brass coins there, the gift of Ymar. Their '''legends''', like their faces, had worn away; and they were dark with verdigris — in appearance precisely the ancient things they were.}} #: {{syn|en|inscription}} # A [[musical]] [[composition]] set to a poetical story. # {{lb|en|naval}} The design and specification of a vessel. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1929|title=Journal of the American Society of Naval Engineers, Inc|page=304 |passage=The '''legend''' displacement on the basis then in use was 48,000 tons, the corresponding standard displacement as defined by the Washington Treaty being 47,540 tons.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=Alan Raven; John Roberts|title=British Battleships of World War Two: The Development and Technical History of the Royal Navy's Battleships and Battlecruisers from 1911 to 1946|page=63 |passage=The '''legend''' and sketch designs were submitted to the Board on 27th March 1916 and, after examining a model and the drawings, the Sea Lords generally favoured proposal 'B'; the extra weight involved being acceptable.}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|legendic|legendist|legendization|legendize|legendless|legendmaker|legendry|sublegend |legend in one's own lunchtime
